newsitem.title: USA: Foreigners invested $480 bln in U.S. last year.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners invested $480 bln in U.S. last year.

text.p: Foreign purchases of U.S. securities and direct investment reached a record $480 billion last year, with Treasury bonds and notes a favored buy, the Securities Industry Association said Friday.
Last year's total pushed foreign holdings in U.S. securities, such as stocks and bonds, to more than $2.4 trillion, "underscoring long-term confidence in the U.S. economy," the association said.
The 1996 figure comprised $384 billion in purchases of U.S. securities and $96 billion in direct investment. The previous yearly record was $292.1 billion, set in 1995.

Total foreign investor holdings of U.S. Treasury securities rose to more than $1.1 trillion. That figure was up nearly a third from the $862 billion held at the start of 1996 and double the amount four years ago.
"Of Treasury notes and bonds privately held, foreign investors now own 33.2 percent, well over the 26.2 percent high of 1978," the statement said.
At the end of 1996, Japan held $277.9 billion and Britain $190.1 billion in Treasury securities. China was in fifth place with $46.6 billion.
U.S. purchases of foreign stocks totaled more than $57.9 billion last year, the second-highest level ever. The record is $62.7 billion in 1993.
U.S. investors put about $13 billion in emerging markets, with Asia getting $8.1 billion of the investment.
